title: Construction workers: building the nation without a roof of their own
author: Editorial Desk
summary: The Akhil Bharatiya Construction Mazdoor Mahasangh and the welfare boards.
body:
Construction is one of the largest employers in the unorganised sector. BMS has a dedicated federation, the **Akhil Bharatiya Construction Mazdoor Mahasangh**.

## The legal framework

The **Building and Other Construction Workers (Regulation of Employment and Conditions of Service) Act, 1996** and the cess law of the same year require employers to pay a cess of one per cent of the cost of construction. The money is used by **State welfare boards** for registered workers' benefits: education grants, medical help, maternity benefit, pension and accident cover. These laws are now part of the new Labour Codes.

## Persistent problems

- Large amounts of **unspent cess** in some States, reported over the years in official and parliamentary documents.
- Slow **registration** of workers and renewal of cards.
- **Diversion of funds** away from the purpose of the cess.
- Poor **safety** on construction sites.

## What BMS says

BMS has asked that welfare board funds be used only for workers, that registration be simple, and that site safety be enforced. The federation has also asked for a **national register** that follows the worker when she moves between States.

For construction workers, a card is not a favour. It is the key to the benefits that their own work has paid for.
